intro: Chat Guard starts in Observe mode. Optional enforcement is fail-closed, capped, platform-aware, and requires both creator approval and one approved triggerless Streamer.bot action.

sections.title: 1. Start safely
sections.description: Select platforms and keep simulations excluded during normal use.
sections.notice: Begin with enforcement disabled and mode set to Observe. Test samples never cause moderation.

sections.title: 2. Optional enforcement
sections.description: Warn in source chat or use the approved provider controller for delete, timeout, or ban.
sections.notice: YouTube has no delete-message method in Streamer.bot. TikTok is warning-only. Unsupported operations fail closed and are recorded, never substituted with a stronger action.

sections.title: 3. Trusted viewers
sections.description: Use stable platform IDs and normalized roles to avoid display-name impersonation.

sections.title: 4. Content and link signals
sections.description: Literal terms, normalized domain policy, link count, caps, repeated-character, and length rules.

sections.title: 5. Repeated messages
sections.description: Flag the same normalized message from the same stable account within a short bounded window.

sections.title: 6. Privacy and retention
sections.description: Limit private incident and repeat-detection state.
sections.notice: Chat Guard never writes message text, names, avatars, or platform account IDs to its state. It stores salted hashes, platform, time, rule IDs, and simulation status only.
